ARCHITECTURE.mechanism1: ExpertVerifierInput.governedEvidence: { sourceId, text }[] — 'as supplied to the first pass. Never re-fetched, never re-selected.' sourceId is the canonical identifier.
ARCHITECTURE.mechanism2: the FIRST PASS already binds model claims to those ids — expert-prompt.ts:1055 enumerates supplied sourceIds into the wire schema, expert-normalization.ts:263 refuses EVIDENCE_SOURCE_UNKNOWN
ARCHITECTURE.whatSection194Did: applied the established first-pass evidence-binding pattern to the verifier path, using the closed-set-by-exact-string-equality discipline v3 already uses for bindingFactKey
ARCHITECTURE.representation: regulatoryBasis { reliance: NONE | SUPPLIED_GOVERNED_EVIDENCE, sourceIds: string[], proposition: string|null }, required on every verdict so silence about reliance is impossible
ARCHITECTURE.whyPropositionIsIncluded: deterministic enforcement does not need it; GOVERNABILITY does. Without it a declaration names a source but not the claim, and a reviewer would have to infer the claim from prose — the exact inference problem §194 exists to escape.

notReused.authority_citation: a citation string is a PROPERTY of a governed record, not an identifier — binding to it would let a model type the right characters and self-authorise
notReused.ApprovedKnowledgeRecord_recordId: the verifier never sees records, only governedEvidence[].sourceId; binding to what was actually supplied keeps the closed set verifiable from the request alone, with no registry lookup or database access

ARCHITECTURE.schemaEnumAlternativeConsidered: the first pass enumerates supplied ids INTO the schema, making an invented id provider-side invalid. NOT taken: it makes the schema per-request and the protocol identity hash would stop being a single stable value, which §187-§192 depend on. The same guarantee is obtained at admission via SOURCE_ID_NOT_IN_SUPPLIED_SET.

FAIL_CLOSED_MATRIX.D_reliance_NONE: admitted, subject to every other contract rule
FAIL_CLOSED_MATRIX.zeroGovernedEvidenceSupplied: ANY declared reliance is refused — there is no route by which a verifier supplies the rule from memory

DETERMINISM_NOT_OVERCLAIMED.statement: STRUCTURAL SOURCE BINDING IS NOT LEGAL VALIDATION

HONEST_RESIDUAL: a v3.2 verifier could still write a regulatory-sounding sentence in prose and declare NONE, and be admitted. No deterministic rule catches that — the §193 finding stands. What changes: there is now a legitimate route it declined to use, CLAIMED authority is fail-closed, and an undeclared prose assertion becomes a semantic review item against a NONE declaration rather than a contract hole. This should NOT be described as closing the prose-assertion class.
